full_judgment:
Mr. Borhanuddin, J: This rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why proceedings of Sessions Case No.644 of 2011 arising out of C. R. Case No.1134 of 2010 under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, now pending in the 5th Court of learned Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge, Chittagong, should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts relevant for disposal of the rule are that the opposite party no.1 herein as complainant lodged a petition of complaint before the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Cognizance Court No.2, Chittagong, impleading the petitioner herein as accused alleging inter-alia that the complainant has been performing as Imam of Hail Salamat Ali Jame Mosque for the last 53 years; The accused executed a bainanama on 24.11.2003 for selling land to the complainant and received advance money; But the accused failed to perform his part and to repay the amount issued a cross cheque of taka 11 lacs in favour of the complainant on 30.04.2010; Complainant presented the cheque for encashment in his account on 01.05.2010 but the cheque was dishonoured on 03.05.2010 with an endorsement "insufficient fund"; Complainant informed the matter to the accused who asked him to present the cheque on 27.07.2010 and accordingly the complainant presented the cheque but again the cheque was dishonoured on 29.07.2010 with the same endorsement; Lastly, on the advice of the accused, complainant presented the cheque on 30.08.2010 for encashment but this time also the cheque was dishonoured on 31.08.2010 with the same endorsement; Complainant issued legal notice on 21.09.2010 upon accused but the notice was returned undelivered on 06.10.2010 with 4 remark by the postal authority that the receiver was not found; Complainant published legal notice in the daily "Purba Kone" on 13.10.2010 and 14.10.2010 respectively for payment of the amount; But the accused did not respond; As such, complainant constrained to lodged the petition of complaint which is registered as C. R. Case No.1134 of 2010. 

 3. Learned Magistrate examined the complainant under section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and after taking cognizance of the offence under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act issued summons upon the accused vide order dated 15.11.2010. Accused voluntarily surrendered on 08.02.2012 and obtained bail from the Court below. Being ready, record of the case transmitted in the Court of learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate. Subsequently, case record transferred in the Court of learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge vide order dated 20.03.2011 wherein the case was numbered as Sessions Case No.644 of 2011. The case was again transferred in the 5th Court of learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge for trial vide order dated 29.03.2011. Learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge after receiving the case record fixed 05.05.2011 for charge hearing. The accused filed an application in the Court below on 05.07.2011 under section 265C of the Code of Criminal Procedure for discharge. Upon hearing the application, learned Judge rejected the application vide order dated 27.09.2011 and framed charge against the accused. 

 4. At this stage, the accused as petitioner preferred instant criminal miscellaneous case by filing an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the present rule along with an order of stay. 

 5. Mr. Md. Asrarul Haque, learned advocate appearing for the accused petitioner submits that the complainant has admitted in the complaint petition that he served legal notice upon the accused on 21.09.2010 through postal service but lodged the complainant petition on 15.11.2010 in violation of the provisions of section 138(1)(b)(c) of the Negotiable Instruments Act as such criminal proceeding is liable to be quashed. He also submits that section 138(1)(b) provides for a legal notice but the complainant after serving legal notice on 21.09.2010 again published legal notice in the daily `Purba Kone' on 13.10.2010 and 14.10.2010 in violation of the provisions of law as such the proceeding is liable to be quashed. He further submits that the complainant has admitted in his complaint petition that the legal notice dated 21.09.2010 was returned undelivered on 06.10.2010 with the remark by the postal authority that the receiver was not found which is a good service under Section 27 of the General Clauses Act as such criminal proceeding based on a tainted complaint petition filed beyond the period prescribed by law is liable to be set aside. In support of his submissions, learned advocate referred to the case of Nurul Islam (Md)-Vs-Md. Ali Hossain Miah being dead his heirs Amir Hossain and others, reported in 50 DLR (AD) 114. 

 6. On the other hand, Mr. Mansur Habib learned advocate appearing for the opposite party no. 1 submits that the complainant stated in his complaint petition that the accused deliberately refused to receive the notice in connivance with postal peon as such the complainant was compelled to publish legal notice in the daily "Purbo Kone" which fact can only be determined upon evidence by the trial court as such the rule is liable to be discharged. He also submits that date of receipt legal notice is a disputed question of fact to be ascertained at the time of trial as such the rule is liable to be discharged. In support of his submissions, learned advocate referred to the case of Nizamuddin Mahmood-Vs-Abdu Hamid Bhuiyan and another, reported in 60 DLR(AD)195; the case of Shahjahan (Md)-Vs- State and another, reported in 16 BLC 686 and the case of Noor Jamal-Vs-State and another, reported in 63 DLR 531. 

 11. Section 138(1) of the Negotiable Instruments Act provides that the cheque has to be presented to the bank within a period of 6(six) months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of validity whichever is earlier; the payee or the holder in due course of cheque as the case may be, will make .a demand for the payment of the amount by giving a notice in writing to the drawer of the cheque, within 30 days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding return of the cheque as unpaid and if the drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment to the holder in due course of the cheque within 30 days of the said notice the complainant can lodge complaint petition within one month of the date on which cause of action arose under clause (c) of the Proviso to section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. If we take the statement of the complaint in toto that the first legal notice served on 21.09.2010 which was returned undelivered on 06.10.2010 then also we find that the complaint petition lodged on 15.11.2010 by the complainant is very much within the time prescribed by law. 

 12. Apart from that, it is already settled by our apex court that the date of receipt legal notice is a disputed question of fact to be ascertained at the time of trial and non-disclosure of such fact in the complaint petition cannot render the proceeding liable to be quashed to the great prejudice of the complainant who is entitled to prove his case on evidence. 

 13. In the facts and circumstances of the case and for the reasons stated above, we do not find any merit in the rule. 

 14. Facts and circumstances of the case referred by learned advocate for the accused petitioner are quite distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the case in hand.
